subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: For Claude CLI sessions with an auth profile selected, should the auth epoch track credential identity rather than local credential storage-source presence, and what identity signal is acceptable when Claude CLI exposes no email or accountId?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the safe permanent fix changes the auth/session boundary and could under-detect real account switches if the identity signal is too weak.

options.title: Narrow Claude CLI Identity Policy
options.body: Prefer an internal Claude CLI-specific rule that ignores storage-source presence only when identity is unchanged or fail-closed when identity cannot be proven.

options.title: Adopt Host-Only Direction
options.body: Accept the broader host-owned auth model from the open PR after resolving conflicts and security concerns.

options.title: Keep Current Fail-Closed Behavior
options.body: Leave current behavior in place and document that users should avoid mixed auth-profile/local Claude CLI churn until stronger identity proof exists.

recommendation.title: Narrow Claude CLI Identity Policy
recommendation.body: Prefer an internal Claude CLI-specific rule that ignores storage-source presence only when identity is unchanged or fail-closed when identity cannot be proven.

likelyOwner.reason: The original auth-epoch invalidation behavior and central session reuse path trace back to this feature history.
